column1: Section 0 — Ground Rules (apply to every objective)

column4: Should we score performance for each salesperson, for each DC, or both?
column5: ★ Both — score each SE and each DC
column6: Both, kept — but DC rating treated as high priority; SE grade benchmarked against last year's performance (not just this-month average)
column7: N/A — organisational rule, not a numeric formula. Two independent scores computed: DC_Score (per DC, see BO1-BO5 below) and SE_Score = f(This_Year_Performance, Last_Year_Performance) [benchmark formula TBD]
column10: Confirm exact formula for 'last-year benchmark' comparison for SE scoring

column4: How should we define time periods such as 'this month' or 'last 90 days'?
column5: ★ This month = 1st-to-today · Last month = full previous calendar month · Last 90 days = 90 days before today
column6: Confirmed — 'last 90 days' window (today minus 90 days) is the primary lookback used across objectives
column7: Period_Start = TODAY() − 90; Period_End = TODAY(). This window is the primary lookback referenced wherever an 'average' or 'recent performance' formula is used below.

column4: Partway through the month, should we scale the target down to match days passed?
column5: ★ Yes — scale target down to match days passed
column6: No — always compare against the full month's target (scaling down would weaken the SE's habit of hitting full target early)
column7: Effective_Target = Full_Month_Target (constant all month; NOT Full_Month_Target × Days_Passed ÷ Days_In_Month)

column4: What does a good grade (A-D) mean?
column5: ★ A = best / highest value, D = worst / needs urgent attention
column6: Confirmed — A=best, D=worst, based on: Avg. repayment days, Gross margin (₹), Private Label value, Net revenue value, Gross margin %
column7: N/A — defines grade direction only (A=highest performance, D=lowest), applied uniformly to every grade formula below.

column4: What should we use to measure Private Label sales?
column6: Expanded — track all three measures in parallel: (1) Total value of PL orders (₹) [original ★ default], (2) Number of PL orders placed, (3) Number of distinct DCs buying PL
column7:
PL_Value (₹) = SUM(Order_Line_Value) WHERE Product.Tag="Private Label" AND Order_Date in period.
PL_Order_Count = COUNT(Orders) WHERE Product.Tag="Private Label" AND Order_Date in period.
PL_DC_Count = COUNT(DISTINCT DC_ID) WHERE DC placed ≥1 Private Label order AND Order_Date in period
column10: 1.5's grade cutoffs are defined against PL_Value only — confirm whether PL_Order_Count and PL_DC_Count should feed a composite BO1 score, or remain supplementary signals the Data Agent surfaces alongside the grade without their own cutoffs

column4: What should this month's PL number be compared against?
column6: Overridden — compare against BOTH: (1) average of the last 90 days, and (2) the AOP annual target; AOP parameter itself flexes with weather, new product launches, and sales team headcount on ground
column7: PL_Expected_90d = AVERAGE(PL_Actual) over trailing 90 days; PL_Expected_AOP = AOP_Target_PL (adjusted periodically for weather / new-product / team-size factors). PL_Expected = COMBINE(PL_Expected_90d, PL_Expected_AOP) [combination method TBD — e.g. average of the two, or MAX/MIN]
column10: Define how the 90-day-average expectation and the AOP-target expectation combine into one PL_Expected value

column4: Should we require growth on top of the average, or is matching it enough?
column6: Growth requirement is not a fixed number — instead, require x% growth tied to the AOP target
column7: PL_Expected = AOP_Target_PL × (1 + x%_dynamic)
column10: Data Agent computes the required growth % dynamically per DC/territory from the live AOP growth assumption for that quarter, rather than one fixed percentage

column4: Which products should count as 'Private Label'?
column6: Any product already tagged as Private Label (own product) in the system
column7: Include Order_Line WHERE Product.Tag = "Private Label" — CONFIRMED real field (Data Norm Agent, Source 3h, live query): products_template.business_segment_name = 'PRIVATE LABEL'. Live sample confirms it populates correctly (e.g. NUTRI ONE and GAPL-branded products both tagged PRIVATE LABEL).
column10: Field is now confirmed and build-ready — no further follow-up. Resolves what was previously just "any product tagged Private Label" with no concrete column.

column4: At what performance ratio (actual ÷ expected) should each grade apply?
column7: PL_Ratio = PL_Actual ÷ PL_Expected. Grade = IF(PL_Ratio≥0.80,"A", IF(PL_Ratio≥0.60,"B", IF(PL_Ratio≥0.40,"C","D")))
column10: Confirm treatment for PL_Ratio > 100% (still Grade A, or a higher band?)

column4: What should count as a genuine, valid DC visit?
column5: ★ An in-app check-in at the DC
column6: A visit must include: staying at the DC for at least 10 minutes AND logging a photograph
column7: Valid_Visit = (Visit_Duration_Minutes ≥ 10) AND (Photo_Logged = TRUE). RESOLVED (Data Norm Agent, business decision): no per-visit check-out timestamp exists in the data (task_management_taskdetails has ~1 row per task, one timestamp, no check-out) — so Visit_Duration_Minutes is now a flat, confirmed 45 minutes for every visit, used for both planning and grading. Photo_Logged must be derived from a JSON image array on that same table (at least one entry), never read as a boolean column.
column10: Practical consequence, confirmed not accidental: since 45 ≥ 10, the duration half of Valid_Visit always passes now — grading effectively reduces to Photo_Logged alone. Duration no longer discriminates between visits for BO2 scoring. Worth reconfirming this is the intended long-run outcome, not just an acceptable workaround for a data gap.

column4: What should the target be for number of unique DCs visited (coverage)?
column6: Fixed target — all mapped DCs in the SE's territory must be covered within the month (not a multiplier of last month)
column7: Coverage_Target = COUNT(All Mapped DCs in SE Territory); Coverage_% = COUNT(DISTINCT DCs Visited This Month) ÷ Coverage_Target

column4: What should the target be for total number of visits (effort)?
column6: Variable / not fixed — condition: DC-to-SE mapping must first be corrected (no under-mapping or over-mapping) before an effort multiplier is meaningful
column7: Effort_Target = Last_Month_Total_Visits × Multiplier_Dynamic, computed only after Mapping_Correction_Complete = TRUE
column10: SE Daily Planner Agent checks live DC-to-SE mapping-quality status each query; once mapping is confirmed clean, it derives the multiplier from the SE's trailing 3-month visit trend rather than a fixed 1.25x, and surfaces a mapping-correction alert instead of a target while mapping is still flagged dirty

column4: How should the coverage score and effort score be combined into one?
column6: Weighted average of coverage % and effort % (not multiplication)
column7: BO2_Score = (W1 × Coverage_%) + (W2 × Effort_%), where W1 + W2 = 100%, weights set dynamically
column10: Agent weights Coverage vs. Effort dynamically each query based on whichever is further behind its target that period — the bigger gap gets more weight that day, instead of a fixed split

column4: Minimum number of days before the same DC can be visited again?
column6: 5 days under normal conditions; if the DC has an overdue (OD) balance, timing instead depends on direct DC/SE communication
column7: Revisit_Allowed = (Days_Since_Last_Visit ≥ 5) OR (DC.OD_Status = TRUE AND Agreed_Revisit_Date reached)
column10: Define the OD exception rule precisely (who decides timing, any cap)

column4: After how many days is a DC 'overdue', and how much extra weight can a large DC get?
column5: ★ Overdue after 30 days; large DC counts up to 2× a small DC
column6: Confirmed — overdue after 30 days; large DC capped at 2× weight vs. a small DC
column7: Overdue_Flag = (Days_Since_Last_Visit > 30); Priority_Weight = Base_Weight × Size_Multiplier, where Size_Multiplier = MIN(DC_Size_Ratio, 2.0)

column4: At what score should each grade apply?
column5: ★ Coverage/Effort: A≥1.0 · B≥0.7 · C≥0.4. Visit-priority: A≥1.5 · B≥1.0 · C≥0.5
column6: Confirmed — kept as-is
column7: CovEffort_Grade = IF(BO2_Score≥1.0,"A",IF(BO2_Score≥0.7,"B",IF(BO2_Score≥0.4,"C","D"))). VisitPriority_Grade = IF(Priority_Score≥1.5,"A",IF(Priority_Score≥1.0,"B",IF(Priority_Score≥0.5,"C","D")))

column4: How should we calculate the 'expected' outstanding balance for a DC?
column5: ★ Last month's outstanding, adjusted for this month's sales growth
column6: Confirmed — as above
column7: Expected_Outstanding = Last_Month_Outstanding × (1 + Sales_Growth_%)

column4: How should we group overdue amounts by age?
column7: Bucket = IF(Days_Overdue≤30,"0-30",IF(Days_Overdue≤60,"31-60",IF(Days_Overdue≤90,"61-90","90+")))

column4: How much should each age group count toward the DC's risk score?
column7: Risk_Weight = LOOKUP(Bucket, {"0-30":0.2, "31-60":0.5, "61-90":0.8, "90+":1.0}); DC_Risk_Amount = SUM(Bucket_Amount × Risk_Weight) across all buckets

column4: Should we cap how far the score can move above/below 'expected'?
column6: Confirmed — cap between 50% and 150% of expected
column7: Outstanding_Ratio = MIN(MAX(DC_Risk_Amount ÷ Expected_Outstanding, 0.50), 1.50)

column4: Which unpaid balances should count as 'outstanding'?
column6: Confirmed — all open, unpaid invoices (including disputed amounts)
column7: Outstanding_Amount = SUM(Invoice_Amount) WHERE Invoice_Status = "Open/Unpaid" (no exclusion for disputed or billing-error line items)

column4: At what score should each grade apply?
column6: Confirmed — as above
column7: BO3_Grade = IF(Outstanding_Ratio≥1.0,"A",IF(Outstanding_Ratio≥0.75,"B",IF(Outstanding_Ratio≥0.50,"C","D")))  — formula unchanged from system; ratio direction as originally defined by engine (confirm with engineering if 'higher = better' or 'higher = riskier')
column10: Have engineering confirm the direction of Outstanding_Ratio in the live code, since the questionnaire's own example (80%→B) reads ambiguously against a pure 'more debt = worse' interpretation

column4: If a DC is graded D on Outstanding Payments, should we block new orders until it pays?
column5: ★ 🔒 Yes — block new order booking until balance is cleared
column6: Confirmed — Yes, block new order booking until the balance is cleared
column7: IF DC.BO3_Grade = "D" THEN Block_New_Order = TRUE (cleared only when Outstanding_Amount = 0)

column4: What should this objective mainly measure?
column6: Both — momentum sets the daily priority; reactivation of quiet DCs builds the visit list
column7: BO4_Priority_Score = Momentum (see 4.2); BO4_Visit_List = RANK(DCs, BY Reactivation_Need DESC) WHERE DC.Status = "Quiet/Silent"

column4: How should we measure 'momentum' (speed of sales)?
column6: Sales ÷ all working days (including days with no selling)
column7: Momentum = Total_Sales_This_Period ÷ Total_Working_Days_In_Period (denominator = ALL working days, not just days with a sale)

column4: How should we measure 'spread' (how many DCs are active)?
column5: ★ DCs that bought ÷ total DCs in territory
column6: Number of DCs that bought something, compared against a 12-month base (not current-territory ratio)
column7: Spread_Ratio = COUNT(DISTINCT DCs_With_Purchase_This_Month) ÷ AVERAGE(COUNT(DISTINCT DCs_With_Purchase)) over trailing 12 months

column4: What growth targets (multipliers) should apply?
column6: Category-specific multipliers: Cattle Feed ×1.2 · Crop Nutrition ×1.15 · Crop Protection ×1.2 · Field Crop = depends on seasonality (no fixed multiplier given)
column7: Momentum_Target = Last_Period_Momentum × Category_Multiplier, where Category_Multiplier = LOOKUP(Product_Category, {"Cattle Feed":1.20, "Crop Nutrition":1.15, "Crop Protection":1.20, "Field Crop":Seasonal_Factor[TBD]})
column10: Field Crop multiplier is not fixed — business says it depends on seasonality. Supply the seasonal multiplier table (e.g. Kharif vs. Rabi factors), or confirm the Data Agent should derive it dynamically from historical seasonal averages the way the Agent-Determined items do

column4: At what score should each grade apply?
column6: Confirmed — keep the current (★) cut-offs, no custom thresholds
column7: BO4_Grade = [existing system cut-off logic, unchanged]
column10: The source questionnaire never enumerates BO4's actual current numeric cut-offs the way it does for BO1/BO2/BO3 — engineering should confirm the exact live A/B/C/D values already coded in the system, so this row can be updated with real numbers rather than 'keep current' as a placeholder

column1: Section 5 — Objective 5 (BO5): Long-Term Growth (Farmer Meetings & Onboarding)

column4: What should count as a valid 'farmer meeting'?
column5: ★ Logged meeting with at least ___ farmers present
column6: Two-tier definition — Mega farmer meeting: 50+ farmers · Regular farmer meeting: 10+ farmers
column7: Valid_Meeting = (Attendee_Count ≥ 50 AND Meeting_Type="Mega") OR (Attendee_Count ≥ 10 AND Meeting_Type="Regular")

column4: What should count as a new DC 'successfully onboarded'?
column5: ★ The DC places its first order
column6: Confirmed — DC places its first order
column7: Onboarded = (First_Order_Placed = TRUE)

column4: What should the target be for farmer meetings?
column6: Flat target — 2 Mega farmer meetings per month
column7: Meeting_Target = 2 Mega meetings / month (flat; not scaled by count of PL-active DCs)

column4: What should the target be for new DCs onboarded?
column6: Flat target — 2 new DCs onboarded per month
column7: Onboarding_Target = 2 new DCs / month (flat; not scaled by territory size)

column4: How should farmer meetings and onboarding be weighted against each other?
column7: BO5_Score = 0.50 × Meeting_Score_% + 0.50 × Onboarding_Score_%, where Meeting_Score_% = Meetings_Held ÷ Meeting_Target and Onboarding_Score_% = DCs_Onboarded ÷ Onboarding_Target

column4: How often should this objective be measured?
column6: Monthly
column7: Recalculate BO5_Score on Calculation_Frequency = "Monthly" (was "Weekly")

column1: Section 6 — Rules That Remove a DC From Consideration Entirely

column4: Which DC statuses should be excluded from every list?
column6: Inactive/closed DCs excluded; additionally factor in supply-chain variable cost as an exclusion consideration
column7: Exclude DC WHERE Status IN ("Inactive","Closed") OR Supply_Chain_Cost_Ratio > Dynamic_Outlier_Threshold(route/cluster)
column10: Data Agent computes supply-chain variable cost per DC at query time (freight distance, delivery frequency, order size) and excludes outlier-cost DCs relative to their route/cluster, instead of one fixed ₹ threshold

column4: Minimum days since last visit before a DC can be listed again?
column6: Confirmed — 5 days
column7: Exclude DC FROM all lists WHERE Days_Since_Last_Visit < 5

column4: Should we skip a DC when its crop/product is out of season?
column6: No — cattle feed and other products are used constantly, so no seasonal skip applied
column7: Seasonal_Skip = FALSE (always included; no crop-calendar filter applied to any DC)

column4: Which conditions should completely block a DC from appearing on any list?
column6: For an overdue (OD) DC, the SE should still visit (not fully blocked); only a legal/compliance hold removes the DC from all lists entirely
column7: Full_Block = (DC.Legal_Hold = TRUE); Credit_Blocked/Blacklisted DCs evaluated live via CONFIRMED field (Data Norm Agent, Source 3d, live query): sale_orderrequest.credit_on_hold (boolean) / credit_on_hold_reason — not auto-blocked, evaluated case by case
column10: Agent always blocks DCs under Legal_Hold. For Credit_Blocked/Blacklisted DCs, it now reads the confirmed sale_orderrequest.credit_on_hold / credit_on_hold_reason fields directly (previously described only as "live OD status and SE/DC communication notes" with no concrete source) to decide visit-eligibility case by case

column1: Section 7 — Turning the 5 Objectives Into One Daily Priority

column4: How many objectives should feed into the daily ranking?
column6: Confirmed — top 3 objectives
column7: Ranked_Objectives = TOP 3 objectives BY Objective_Score DESC (per DC or per SE)

column4: How much weight should the 1st, 2nd, 3rd priority objectives get?
column6: Confirmed — 40% / 35% / 25%
column7: Daily_Priority_Score = 0.40 × Score_Rank1 + 0.35 × Score_Rank2 + 0.25 × Score_Rank3

column4: What should the default order of importance be across objectives?
column5: ★ Private Label, Visits, Overall Sales, Outstanding Payments, Long-Term Growth
column6: Custom order confirmed: Outstanding Payments, Private Label Sale, DC Visits, Long-Term Growth
column7: Tie_Break_Order = [Outstanding Payments, Private Label, DC Visits, Long-Term Growth, Overall Sales(position TBD)]
column10: Overall Sales (BO4) is not placed in the order the business gave — only 4 of the 5 objectives are sequenced. Confirm where BO4 sits (e.g. last, since it's excluded here) before this feeds the live tie-break logic

column4: Should any special override rules apply?
column5: ★ (a) Outstanding=D caps Overall Sales at B · ★ (b) If all objectives=D, switch order to Visits, PL, Overall Sales, Outstanding, Long-Term
column6: Rule (b) explicitly confirmed — all-D reorder to Visits, PL, Overall Sales, Outstanding, Long-Term. Rule (a) [Outstanding=D caps Overall Sales at B] not explicitly re-confirmed
column7: Rule_A [applied by default]: IF BO3_Grade="D" THEN BO4_Grade = MIN(BO4_Grade,"B"). Rule_B [confirmed]: IF ALL(BO1..BO5 Grades)="D" THEN Priority_Order = [Visits, PL, Overall Sales, Outstanding, Long-Term]
column10: Agent applies rule (a) by default as a conservative precaution and flags 'applying default override, please confirm' in its output until the business explicitly turns it off

column1: Section 8 — Turning Priorities Into a Realistic Daily Plan

column4: How many objectives per day, and only 1 long activity/day?
column6: Confirmed — max 3 objectives/day; 1 long-cycle activity/day
column7: Max_Objectives_Per_Day = 3; Max_Long_Cycle_Activities_Per_Day = 1 (long-cycle = farmer meeting or onboarding)

column4: What is the SE's daily working capacity?
column6: Custom — 8-hour day = 60 min calls + 7 hrs field
column7: Call_Minutes_Available = 60; Field_Minutes_Available = 7 × 60 = 420; Total_Minutes = 480 (8 hrs)

column4: How long should we assume each activity takes?
column5: ★ Call 6 min · Visit 45 min · Farmer meeting 180 min · Onboarding 120 min
column6: Custom — Call 10 min · Visit 45-60 min · Farmer meeting 180 min (or full day if Mega meeting) · Onboarding 120 min
column7: Call_Duration = 10 min; Visit_Duration = 45–60 min; Meeting_Duration = IF(Meeting_Type="Mega", Full_Day, 180 min); Onboarding_Duration = 120 min

column3: Max DCs per objective per day/week
column4: Max number of DCs per objective, per day or week?
column6: Confirmed — as above
column7: Daily_Plan_Cap = {Visits:6/day, Outstanding:4/day, PL:5/day, Long_Term:2/week}

column4: What conditions qualify a DC to appear on each objective's list?
column5: ★ Visits: not visited in 14 days · Outstanding: balance ≥₹5,000 & overdue ≥30 days · PL: <3 orders in 30 days · Long-Term: had PL sales in last 90 days
column6: Confirmed with one override — Visits: not visited in 14 days (= ★ default) · Outstanding: balance ≥₹20,000 & overdue ≥15 days (overridden from ★ ₹5,000/30 days) · PL: <3 orders in 30 days (= ★ default) · Long-Term: had PL sales in last 90 days (= ★ default)
column7: Qualify_Visits = (Days_Since_Last_Visit > 14); Qualify_Outstanding = (Balance ≥ 20000 AND Days_Overdue ≥ 15); Qualify_PL = (PL_Order_Count_30d < 3); Qualify_LongTerm = (Had_PL_Sale_Last_90d = TRUE)
column10: Outstanding threshold moved from ₹5,000/30 days to a higher balance (₹20,000) but a shorter overdue window (15 days) — worth confirming this is intentional, since it surfaces fewer but larger, more urgent debts rather than more numerous smaller ones

column4: What should count as a 'win' for each objective?
column5: ★ PL=order booked · Visits=completed · Outstanding=payment received OR firm promise-to-pay date · Overall Sales=order placed · Long-Term=meeting held/DC onboarded
column6: Same, except Outstanding = payment received only (promise-to-pay date removed as a qualifying win)
column7: PL_Win=(Order_Booked=TRUE); Visit_Win=(Visit_Completed=TRUE); Outstanding_Win=(Payment_Received=TRUE); Sales_Win=(Order_Placed=TRUE); LongTerm_Win=(Meeting_Held=TRUE OR DC_Onboarded=TRUE)

column4: How should we avoid contacting the same DC too often?
column5: ★ Max 2 attempts/week; wait 2 days after failed call, 3 days after failed visit; -30% priority after 2 attempts
column6: Max 2 attempts per 3-day gap; wait 2 days after a failed call; wait per route-planning schedule (not a fixed day count) after a failed visit; -30% priority after 2 attempts
column7: Max_Attempts = 2 per rolling 3-day window; Wait_After_Failed_Call = 2 days; Wait_After_Failed_Visit = Route_Plan_Schedule (variable); IF Attempts≥2 THEN Priority = Priority × (1 − 0.30)

column4: Are there any other safety rules we should apply?
column5: ★ A visit must happen before booking a PL order
column6: Visit-before-PL-order rule retained; add: maximum discount the SE/system may offer (% not yet specified) and DC approval required in-system before order creation
column7: REQUIRE Visit_Completed=TRUE BEFORE Order_Booking("Private Label"); Discount_% ≤ [Max_Discount_Dynamic]; REQUIRE DC_Approval_In_System=TRUE BEFORE Order_Creation
column10: Agent applies the last-approved discount ceiling for that DC's category as a conservative default, and routes any exception to a human for approval before the SE is told to offer it — this one stays close to a safety rule even though it's agent-assisted

column4: What is the maximum distance an SE may travel across all visits in a month?
column6: 1,600 km per SE per month — CORRECTED: ADVISORY / INFORMATIONAL ONLY, not a hard cap. The real hard constraint governing travel is time-based: max 3 hours (180 min) of travel time in the field per day (see Routing Agent R1.2), not a distance figure.
column7: Total_Monthly_Travel_KM = SUM(google_distance) — tracked and shown, never blocks route generation or rejects a plan. Distance is advisory throughout; only Field_Minutes_Available (420 min) and the 180-min travel-time ceiling are hard caps.
column10: Corrected per Routing Agent OQ-4/13 and direct business confirmation: previously documented here as a hard reject/re-sequence trigger, which was wrong — 1,600 km/month (and the related 80 km/day figure) are informational only

column4: How many tasks maximum can an SE be assigned in a single day?
column6: 5 tasks maximum per day — CLARIFIED: this is a CEILING, not a guaranteed flat count. It's achievable only in the best case, when travel time between that day's actual stops stays well under the 180-min ceiling (R1.2). As travel time grows toward that ceiling, fewer visit-slots fit in the remaining budget and the effective number of tasks goes down — see Routing Agent R1.4 for the live formula.
column7: COUNT(Daily_Task_List) ≤ 5 at the BO Scoring Engine stage (visit-duration-only math, no travel time yet). The Routing Agent re-checks this against REAL travel time between the specific candidate stops (Haversine-based) and may trim it further — see R1.4, GR-R5. 5 is a nominal upper bound handed downstream, not the guaranteed daily count.
column10: Reconcile with 8.1's 'max 3 objectives/day' and 8.4's per-objective caps (Visits≤6/day, PL≤5/day) — those predate this global 5-task cap. Recommended reading: 8.1 governs which objective categories feed the candidate pool, this 8.10 caps actual DC engagements (which may bundle multiple objectives per 8.12), and the Routing Agent is the stage that actually enforces the travel-time-driven reduction

column4: What happens to the rest of the daily plan if a Farmer Meeting is scheduled? And can a DC Visit day also carry a Farmer Meeting?
column6: Mutually exclusive, both directions: if the system proposes a DC Visit day, no Farmer Meeting exists in that day's plan, and if a Farmer Meeting is scheduled, no DC Visit exists in that day's plan
column7:
IF Day_Type = "Farmer Meeting": Daily_Task_List = [Farmer_Meeting_Task] only, DC_Visit tasks excluded.
IF Day_Type = "DC Visit": Daily_Task_List = [DC_Visit_Task, ...] only, Farmer_Meeting_Task excluded.
Day_Type is decided once per day by Layer 1 before either branch runs — never both in the same Daily_Task_List
column10: 8.1 previously allowed 1 long-cycle activity alongside other objectives on the same day — this supersedes that: the two Visit Types (per the "Visit Type to Purpose (System)" sheet) are now a hard either/or for the whole day, not just a cap on how many long-cycle activities fit

column4: Can a single DC Visit carry more than one Visit Purpose in the same meeting?
column6: Yes — a single DC Visit can bundle multiple Visit Purposes from the real system list (Promise To Bill (P2B), Promise To Pay / Collection, Query Resolution, Sale, Stock at DC) in one meeting, as mapped in the "Visit Type & Purpose Mapping" and "Visit Type to Purpose (System)" sheets, rather than requiring a separate visit per purpose
column7:
Matched_Purposes(DC) = subset of {Promise_To_Bill, Promise_To_Pay_Collection, Query_Resolution, Sale, Stock_at_DC} that apply this visit:
  IF DC ∈ Qualify_Outstanding (8.5) → include Promise_To_Pay_Collection (and Promise_To_Bill where a billing commitment is the ask)
  IF DC ∈ Qualify_PL or Qualify_Visits-driven order opportunity → include Sale
  Query_Resolution and Stock_at_DC may be logged ad hoc by the SE regardless of what the algorithm pre-loaded
Task_Weight(DC) = 1 regardless of |Matched_Purposes(DC)| — one DC Visit = one task slot, however many purposes it carries
column10: Farmer Meeting has its own multi-purpose set (Farmer App, Farmer Credit, Hyperlocal Input/Service, Insurance, Other/Private Label Product Promotion, Sampoorna) that can similarly co-occur within one meeting — this bundling behavior applies within a Farmer Meeting too, it just never crosses over into a DC Visit on the same day per 8.11
